China First.note: Blank stands. The February 2019 mission report (P129713) was opened: it calls the firm only 'l'entreprise China First', puts its site camp on avenue Gazumbu and its administrative office at avenue Maman Yemo no. 419, Quartier Industriel, Kolwezi, and notes it had produced a site environmental plan for the same project at Kisangani. That is what it did at project sites, not a description of the firm; the document states no sector beyond contracting, no ownership, no size and no nationality. Searches returned only unrelated firms with 'China First' in longer names, which would be different entities.

Unité de Coordination des Projets (UCoP).desc: A project coordination unit of the Democratic Republic of Congo, set up by presidential decree in September 2003 for an emergency reconstruction programme and extended by later decrees to further donor-financed projects. It sat under the authority of the Ministry of Planning, was built as a light structure of a central coordination office, an operations directorate and an administrative and financial directorate, and had no environmental or social specialist of its own.

sources.title: Financing Agreement for Grant H282-ZR (Conformed)
République démocratique du Congo - Projet d'urgence de réhabilitation urbaine et sociale : Cadre de politique de réinstallation
Congo - Grants for Emergency Urban and Social Rehabilitation Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report)

Régie de Distribution d’Eau (REGIDESO).desc: The state water company of the Democratic Republic of Congo, wholly owned by the Congolese state and supervised by the ministries of Energy and Water Resources and of Portfolio. It began in 1939 as a combined water and electricity board, became a limited company in 2014, and had 695,303 subscribers and about 4,613 permanent staff at the end of 2022.

sources.title: Rapport annuel REGIDESO 2023

Office de Voirie et Drainage (OVD).desc: A Congolese public body inside the Ministry of Infrastructure, Public Works and Reconstruction that builds and maintains the country's urban roads, mainly in the provincial capitals. It manages 89 percent of the paved roads in Kinshasa.

sources.title: Etude du plan directeur de transport urbain de Kinshasa

Ministerio de Ambiente, Vivienda y Desar.desc: A Colombian government ministry that until 2011 handled both environment and housing, water and land-use policy. Law 1444 of 2011 separated its housing, land-use and water and sanitation duties, which went to the Ministry of Housing, City and Territory, and renamed the rest the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development.

sources.title: Decreto 3570 de 2011
sources.publisher: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible, Colombia

Fondo Financiero de Proyectos de Desarro.desc: A Colombian state-owned financial body that prepares and manages public development projects for national and local government. Decree 495 of 2019 renamed it Empresa Nacional Promotora del Desarrollo Territorial (ENTerritorio); it is an industrial and commercial state enterprise of a financial character, attached to the National Planning Department and supervised by the financial regulator.

sources.title: Decreto 495 de 2019

Departamento de La Guajira.desc: A department of Colombia, whose municipalities include Riohacha, Maicao and Uribia. The national statistics office projected its population at 1,002,394 for 2022, on projections from the 2018 census.

sources.title: InfoDane: Riohacha, La Guajira
sources.publisher: Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística (DANE), Colombia

Aguas de La Guajira S.A. E.S.P..desc: A private joint-stock utility company that ran the drinking water and sewerage service in Riohacha, Colombia, from the start of the 2000s. Its majority shares were sold on 13 September 2014 and it was renamed Avanzadas Soluciones de Acueducto y Alcantarillado S.A. E.S.P. (ASAA).

sources.title: Evaluación integral de prestadores: Avanzadas Soluciones de Acueducto y Alcantarillado S.A. E.S.P. (Riohacha)
sources.publisher: Superintendencia de Servicios Públicos Domiciliarios, Colombia

Fundación MANA.note: Blank stands. The project's own Evaluación Social y Plan de Reasentamiento Indígena (June 2011, P096965) was opened: it records only that the foundation signed contract No. 013 of 31 March 2009 with the Gobernación de La Guajira for studies and designs in the area of the Riohacha lagoon and fielded a team of social staff from 3 April 2009. That is what it did on this project, not what the body is. No register entry, site or news page naming Fundación MANA could be opened, so its sector, ownership and size are unverified.

Agence Djiboutienne d'Execution des Trav.desc: A Djiboutian public agency whose mandate was to carry out public works by labour-intensive methods, working as a contract-management agency on donor-financed projects. It no longer operates under that name: it was merged with the Social Development Fund into the Agence Djiboutienne de Développement Social, a public administrative establishment created by Decree No. 0025 of 8 January 2008 and supervised by the State Secretariat for Solidarity.

sources.title: Djibouti - Flood Emergency Rehabilitation Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report)
About ADDS

Housing Fund of the Ministry of Urban De.desc: A Djiboutian state housing body (Fonds de l'Habitat). As of 2018 it was one of two bodies, alongside the Société Immobilière de Djibouti, through which a delegate ministry for housing created in 2011 carried out public housing policy; it had focused on building homes for lower-income households and preparing plots for low-income housing, and the same report says it was then being relaunched as the Agency for Urban Rehabilitation and Social Housing.

sources.title: Home improvement: the provision of housing remains a critical component of development plans (The Report: Djibouti 2018)

Instituto Nacional de Recursos Hidráulic.desc: The Dominican Republic's national water agency, created as an autonomous state body by Law No. 6 of 1965 and based in Santo Domingo. It plans and builds river works, dams, irrigation systems and hydroelectric plants, runs the national irrigation systems, and assesses the country's water resources.

sources.title: Ley No. 6 que crea el Instituto Nacional de Recursos Hidráulicos

Hanson – Rodríguez, S.R.L..note: Blank stands. The corrective resettlement plans of 11 March 2016 and the completion report (22 April 2017, P109932) were opened: they call it an 'empresa consultora' holding the project's technical supervision, designated by INDRHI, and record that its Lot 1 supervision contract overran by 73.31 percent. That restates its role on the case and describes a contract, not the firm. No register entry, site, award page or news report naming Hanson – Rodríguez, S.R.L. could be opened, so its business, ownership and size are unverified.

Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Munici.desc: The municipal government of the canton of Manta, Ecuador, whose powers under the country's local government code (COOTAD) include local planning and land use, water supply and sewerage, waste collection, traffic and transport, urban works, and risk management. The 2022 national census counted 258,697 people in the canton.

sources.title: Informe de gestión GAD Manta 2024
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del Cantón Manta

Empresa Pública Aguas de Manta (EPAM).desc: A public company of the canton of Manta, Ecuador, created by municipal ordinance in 2010 and run by a five-member board chaired by the mayor. It supplies drinking water and runs the sewerage, stormwater and wastewater treatment systems for the canton; a 2020 ordinance replaced the founding rule without creating a new company and gave it the longer name Empresa Pública Municipal de Agua Potable, Alcantarillado, Manejo Pluvial y Depuración de Residuos Líquidos del cantón Manta.

sources.title: Ordenanza 023-2020 sustitutiva de creación de la EP Aguas de Manta
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Descentralizado Municipal del Cantón Manta

Commission Nationale des Travaux d'Intér.desc: A Gabonese national commission established by ministerial order (arrêté) No. 00007/PRIMPPD of 4 January 2006 to carry out projects in the public interest on behalf of the government, regional and local administrations, non-governmental organisations and donors. It is directed by its permanent secretary and its size varies with the workload, with a minimum of six key staff working across several projects.

Municipal Development Fund of Georgia (M.desc: A Georgian state body established in 1997, a legal entity under public law, whose work is coordinated by the Ministry of Infrastructure. It invests in local infrastructure and services, including water and sewage networks, schools and kindergartens, homes for displaced people, and works at tourist and cultural heritage sites.

sources.title: Our History

National Agency for Cultural Heritage Pr.desc: A Georgian state agency set up by presidential decree in 2008 to preserve, protect and promote the country's movable and immovable monuments. It keeps the register and inventory of monuments and sites, documents intangible heritage, gives expert opinion on rehabilitation work, and runs museum-reserves including Vardzia and Uplistsikhe.

sources.title: Georgia national policy report: organisations (HEREIN European Heritage Network)

Roads Department of Georgia.desc: The Georgian state body that designs, builds, rehabilitates and maintains the country's roads of international and intrastate importance under Georgia's Law on Roads, with the Ministry of Infrastructure setting policy and hearing appeals against its decisions. A 2023 presentation by the department put the network in its care at 6,970 km, of which 1,511 km are international roads, and its staff at 238; municipalities keep the local roads.

sources.title: Law of Georgia on Roads (No. 585, 1994, consolidated)
Roads Department of Georgia: vision presentation

Lands Commission, Ghana.desc: Ghana's national land administration body, established under Article 258 of the 1992 Constitution and the Lands Commission Act, 2008 (Act 767), and able to sue and be sued in its own name. Alongside public and vested lands and the registration of deeds and land instruments, it sets standards for and regulates surveying and mapping of the country and provides land valuation, through four divisions.

sources.title: About Us

Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources,.desc: The Ghanaian government ministry whose stated mission is the sustainable management and use of the country's lands, forests, wildlife and mineral resources. It works through three sub-sectors and oversees bodies including the Lands Commission, the Forestry Commission, the Minerals Commission, the Ghana Geological Survey Authority and the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands.

sources.title: Our Ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Ghana

Ministry of Information and Communicatio.desc: A Gambian government ministry for communications, which held that name from 2011, when the Ministry of Communications, Information and Information Technology was renamed, until 2022, when it was split into the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy and the Ministry of Information. The same line of ministries began as the Department of State for Communications and Information Technology in 2002.

sources.title: MOCDE Infographic
sources.publisher: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy, The Gambia

Gambia Telecommunications Company Limite.desc: The Gambia's state telecoms operator, incorporated under the Companies Act 1955 as amended, with 99 percent of its shares held by the Gambian government and 1 percent by the Gambia Ports Authority. It provides landline voice service and data services including fibre and ADSL, and its draft 2022 accounts show revenue of 455 million dalasi and a loss of 245 million dalasi; a cited audit of its accounts put permanent staff at 1,046 at the end of 2017.

sources.title: Performance Audit Report on Service Delivery by Gamtel

SAL Consult Limited.note: Blank stands. The resettlement plan it wrote (RP1149, May 2011, P122402) was opened: it gives only the firm's name as author and a post box address, P O Box GP20200, Accra. A further search returned only third-party aggregator listings (Devex, DevelopmentAid, ZoomInfo, ecohubmap). No company site, register entry or news page describing the firm could be opened, so its sector, ownership and size are unverified.

Secretaría de Infraestructura y Servicio.desc: A Honduran government ministry responsible for policy on housing, public works, the road, urban and transport systems, public enterprises and the public works concession regime. Its powers were restated by Legislative Decree 266-2013, the law on streamlining public administration.

sources.title: Informe 054-2021-DFEP-INSEP

Unité Centrale d'Exécution, Ministère de.desc: The unit inside Haiti's Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications through which the ministry procures and carries out works financed by outside lenders, running the tenders and the contracts. A 2025 notice has it inviting electronic bids, through its own bidding platform, for World Bank-financed drainage works at Cap-Haïtien.

sources.title: Avis d'appel d'offres: travaux d'assainissement de la ville du Cap-Haïtien (projet RUTAP), 26 April 2025
Official Documents - Financing Agreement for Grant D136-HT, Second Additional Financing, Haiti (definition of UCE)

Comité Permanent d'Acquisitions à l'Amia.desc: The Haitian state body that handles expropriations, sitting at the Ministry of Economy and Finance. It identifies the people whose property is affected, has their titles checked with the tax directorate and a notary, values land and buildings against a price framework that it updates, then pays. It grew out of the Comité d'Évaluation, which had operated at the public works ministry since 1994 and had stopped functioning.

sources.title: Cadre de politique de réinstallation, Haiti Digital Acceleration Project (P171976)

Royal Caribbean.desc: Royal Caribbean Group, a cruise company listed on the New York Stock Exchange as RCL, which owns the Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea Cruises brands and half of a joint venture operating TUI Cruises and Hapag-Lloyd Cruises. It reported total revenue of 16.5 billion dollars and net income of 2.9 billion dollars for 2024, and 66 ships in service at the start of 2025.

sources.title: Royal Caribbean Group Reports 2024 Results (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)

Directorate General of Highways, Ministr.desc: The directorate general inside Indonesia's Ministry of Public Works and Housing that draws up and carries out policy on roads, including the national road network, and works through regional national road implementation units (Balai Pelaksanaan Jalan Nasional). Its own condition survey put the national road network at 47,603 km in the first half of 2023.

sources.title: Buku Kondisi Jalan Nasional 2023 Semester I
sources.publisher: Direktorat Jenderal Bina Marga, Kementerian PUPR, Indonesia

Peraturan Menteri PUPR No. 11/PRT/M/2016

Commissioner of Revenue Administration,.desc: The head office of the revenue arm of the government of Tamil Nadu in India, working in each district through the District Collector. The Board of Revenue was abolished during 1980 and its functions taken over by three new commissionerates, now five; the department keeps land records and handles mutations, issues certificates such as community, income and legal heirship certificates, acts as custodian of government property, and distributes relief in disasters.

sources.title: Mission
sources.publisher: Commissionerate of Revenue Administration and Disaster Management, Government of Tamil Nadu

Ahwaz Water and Wastewater Company.desc: The water and wastewater company for the city of Ahwaz, Iran, one of thirty-three provincial and city water and wastewater companies that provide water and wastewater services in a sector run under the Ministry of Energy, and the borrower of a World Bank loan on-lent by the state in 2004. It is headed by a general assembly and a managing director; audited accounts for the four years to 2003/04 show it making net losses, with water losses falling from 46 percent in 1999/2000 to 37.7 percent in 2002/03.

Iran - Ahwaz and Shiraz Water Supply and Sanitation Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report)

State Commission for Roads and Bridges,.desc: A commission within Iraq's Ministry of Construction and Housing, based in Baghdad, which handled the federal government's road and bridge works outside the Kurdistan region, where the General Directorate of Roads and Bridges did so. The government later restructured it: the ministry became the Ministry of Construction, Housing and Public Municipalities and the body was made a department of it, the Roads and Bridges Directorate, responsible for planning and managing the national road network and expressways.

sources.title: Loan Agreement for Loan 8322-IQ, Iraq Transport Corridors Project (Closing Package)
Iraq - Transport Corridors Project (Implementation Completion and Results Report)

Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Jor.desc: The Jordanian government ministry for tourism and for the country's archaeological heritage. Tourism was first handled by a bureau from 1953, was raised to a ministry by royal decree in 1967, and the ministry took its present name in 1989, when the Department of Antiquities was brought under it.

sources.title: Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities: General Information

Council for Development and Reconstructi.desc: A Lebanese public institution created by legislative decree No. 5 of 31 January 1977 and answering directly to the Council of Ministers. It draws up national development and reconstruction plans, runs the projects, and may take domestic and foreign loans; it reported about 10.9 billion dollars of projects carried out or under way between 1992 and 2016.

sources.title: CDR after 40 years: USD 11 billion of projects

Mirai Construction Company Limited.note: Blank stands. The project's Abbreviated Land Acquisition Plan (20 February 2007, P111708) was opened: it names the firm only as the holder of the Dennery Coastal Protection Phase 1 and 2 contract at EC$6,683,042.53. No company site, register entry, award page or news report naming the firm could be opened, so its sector, ownership and size are unverified.

Smith Warner International.desc: A coastal engineering and coastal zone management consultancy founded in 1995 by David Smith and Philip Warner with one office in Kingston, Jamaica, and now also offices in St Lucia, Trinidad and Tobago, and Vancouver. Its site says it has 30 full-time professionals and lists consulting and construction services.

sources.title: About Us

Ministry of Public Works and Transport,.desc: A ministry of the government of Lesotho. The country's Roads Directorate began as a department inside it and was established as a separate corporate body by the Roads Directorate Act of 2010.

sources.title: Roads maintenance kicks off
Government Ministries

Agency for State Roads.desc: The state body for the national road network of Macedonia, now North Macedonia. Amendments to the Law on Public Roads of 11 July 2008 created it as legal successor to the Fund for National and Regional Roads, which had run the network from 1996, under the name Agency for Public Roads; a law of 27 December 2012 replaced it, by then named Agency for State Roads, with the Public Enterprise for State Roads, which took over its staff, property, assets and archives.

sources.title: History
sources.publisher: Public Enterprise for State Roads, North Macedonia

Customs Administration.desc: North Macedonia's customs service, founded on 14 April 1992 with the adoption of the Law on the Customs Administration and holding its own legal personality. It carries out customs supervision, customs clearance and customs control of goods, is the country's sole body competent for administering excise duties, and reported collecting 131,634.3 million denars, about 2.14 billion euro, from imports and domestic trade in 2025.

sources.title: Our Role
sources.publisher: Customs Administration of the Republic of North Macedonia

sources.title: Annual Report 2025
sources.publisher: Customs Administration of the Republic of North Macedonia

Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi JSC.desc: A Mongolian coal mining company that holds four of the five licences over the Tavan Tolgoi coking coal deposit. The state holding company Erdenes Mongol owns 65.2 percent of it, about 14.8 percent of its shares were handed to every Mongolian citizen, and 20 percent is unallocated pending a planned share offering; it reported revenue of 1,194 billion tugrik and 717 permanent staff in 2017.

sources.title: Wild Growth: An Assessment of Erdenes Mongol

Ministry of Finance of Mongolia.desc: Mongolia's finance ministry. Its medium-term government debt management strategy for 2026-2028, which the Law on Debt Management requires to be approved every three years together with the medium-term fiscal framework, puts total government debt at 33,384.6 billion tugrik, or 41.8 percent of GDP, at the end of 2024, on preliminary figures.

sources.title: Medium-Term Government Debt Management Strategy 2026-2028

Administracao de Infra-estruturas de Agu.desc: A Mozambican public institute created by Decree 19/2009 and reorganised by Decree 112/2020, with Category A status, its own legal personality and administrative, financial and asset autonomy. It is the main counterpart of the public and private operators of public water supply and of wastewater and stormwater drainage systems, manages investment programmes in them, and can delegate their operation by management contract or concession.

sources.title: Decreto n.º 112/2020, de 29 de Dezembro

Companhia dos Caminhos de Ferro da Beira.desc: A railway concession company set up to rehabilitate and run Mozambique's Beira rail corridor, including the 317 km Machipanda line from Beira to Zimbabwe's railways and the Sena line north to the Moatize coal mines, under a 25-year concession. The consortium of RITES and IRCON won the concession in May 2004 and held 26 and 25 percent; the Government of Mozambique held the remaining 49 percent through the rail parastatal CFM.

sources.title: RITES-IRCON consortium takes over Beira rail corridor in Mozambique
